summary: Operational repair can release a revoked legacy runtime start only after its owner daemon proves its vanished pid-less PTY has no remaining systemd seat/server units or operation-labelled processes

replay.detail: No replay; the operator reviews a fresh st3.operational-repair.v0 plan and applies its exact token.

schema.detail: No database schema change. Repair uses the normal producer-closed cleanup transition and retains a repair.applied receipt.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: The repair plan gains revoked-legacy-runtime-start items and repeatable exact subject/class filters. Filtered approval tokens embed their canonical filter and require an upgraded daemon; the CLI refuses a daemon that ignores filters. Existing unfiltered tokens remain valid. Native operation-owned launch retirement is unchanged; registry rows are not deleted.

downtime.detail: No interruption beyond the normal daemon rollout.

manual.detail: On the owning Linux host, review st repair dry-run --class revoked-legacy-runtime-start --subject SUBJECT --json (repeat --subject for each approved seat), then apply its exact token with st repair apply TOKEN --json. Apply recomputes only that selected set; any missing or changed physical or writer-owned evidence refuses the repair.

recovery.detail: No destructive recovery or ledger edits. Keep the receipt and repeat dry-run to confirm the repaired start no longer retains admission.
